glossary.definition: AI alignment is the effort to make sure an AI system's actual behavior matches what its developers and users truly intend and value, especially as systems become more capable and autonomous. It's similar to raising a very powerful, very literal-minded genie: you have to be extremely careful that what you asked for is actually what you wanted, because a technically-correct-but-unintended interpretation of an instruction can go badly wrong. It covers everything from a chatbot politely refusing a harmful request to long-term research on keeping far more capable future systems safe.

items.title: Blue Planet III is keeping the rough edges in the age of AI
items.summary: BBC's Blue Planet III is looking to prove its authenticity by leaving in the less-than-perfect shots. Previous incarnations of the nature series were defined by their gorgeous, crystal-clear footage that seemed almost too good to be real. But one dead giveaway of AI is when things look too polished and seamless. To counter that, Blue Planet III goes warts and all.

items.title: The AI graveyard: a running list of projects and startups that didn’t make it
items.summary: From Apple's repeatedly delayed Siri AI to OpenAI's messy "super app" launch, here's a look at the AI projects that shut down or missed expectations. Relay, an AI-powered workflow automation tool built as an alternative to Zapier, shut down entirely in August. The product let users automate email and task workflows using AI agents, but as OpenAI, Google, and other larger platforms built similar automation directly into their own tools, five-year-old Relay struggled to hold on to a reason to exist as a stand-alone product. ai filed for bankruptcy just five years after launching.

items.title: Pennsylvania will require labels on AI-generated ads
items.summary: On Thursday, Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro signed the Artificial Intelligence Deceptive Advertising Act into law, requiring disclosures on AI-generated ads. The law requires any ad - whether it's a still image, video, audio, or text - that "has been significantly modified or generated by artificial intelligence" to include a label in the same format as the ad itself. That applies to TV commercials from multi-billion-dollar companies , as well as restaurants' ugly, crowded flyers about their wing specials. Pennsylvania is one of the first states to require disclosures on AI content.

items.title: Block’s new voice model sounds eerily human
items.summary: Block said that the voice model can run locally on a MacBook M4 Max Jack Dorsey’s Block released a new voice model out of the company’s research lab that runs locally and sounds strangely human with its expressions like laughs, pauses, and cries. The company said the model, called Dessa, is trained fully on human speech and a single NVIDIA GPU rack. Dessa is a full-duplex model, which means it can talk and listen at the same time, just like the GPT-Live model OpenAI released earlier this year .

items.title: Three fired OpenAI safety researchers say they were never told what they actually leaked
items.summary: The three OpenAI safety researchers who were fired, Tomek Korbak, Mikita Balesni, and Jasmine Wang, are publicly pushing back against allegations from their former employer. They deny sharing confidential information and see a connection to their advocacy for AI systems that are easier to scrutinize. The researchers say OpenAI never told them in writing which information they allegedly mishandled. Tomek Korbak, Mikita Balesni, and Jasmine Wang deny sharing confidential information, question the official reasoning behind their termination, and suspect a connection to their advocacy for more transparent AI systems.

items.title: The PHP Meltdown Shows How AI Makes Bugs More Exploitable
items.summary: Security researchers used AI tools to help uncover years-old vulnerabilities in the PHP web scripting language. Then the AI-assisted attacks began. As security teams and web admins scrambled this week to patch newly public PHP bugs , criminal hackers quickly attempted to exploit the flaws in the wild. Millions of exploitation attempts hit within hours of the vulnerabilities being published, according to analysis from Cloudflare—unsurprising given broad access to AI tools that can make it easier for attackers to quickly exploit flaws.

items.title: DrizzVision’s AI App Testing Ambition Meets Reality
items.summary: Mobile app testing is often a race against change. A redesigned screen, a renamed button or an unexpected pop-up can break an automated test, forcing developers to spend time fixing scripts instead of testing functionality. Bengaluru-based DrizzVision wants AI to make that process less brittle. Its agent, Fathom, uses visual models to interpret app screens and execute tests from natural-language instructions, rather than relying solely on predefined element identifiers.

items.title: Moonshot AI launches new flagship Kim K3.1 Pro model with 3T parameters
items.summary: Moonshot AI today introduced Kim K3.1 Pro, a large language model that can perform some tasks better than Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra. The LLM is a post-trained, or upgraded, version of an algorithm that the Chinese artificial intelligence company released in July. The latter model, Kimi K3, comprises 896 individual neural networks with 3 trillion parameters. It only activates 16 of those neural networks at any given time to minimize inference costs.

items.title: Google will pay people to use less electricity so its data centers can use more
items.summary: Google has an answer to some of the electricity supply problems that data center construction is causing : It has signed an agreement with energy supplier Voltus to build what it’s calling a 1-gigawatt virtual power plant, expanding on an earlier 100 megawatt deal the two signed earlier this year. This power plant is virtual in the sense that it doesn’t generate any electricity itself, but aggregates so-called flexible grid capacity into one central resource that can be deployed at times of peak demand. This flexible capacity can be in the form of batteries or of load-shedding: asking others to temporarily stop consuming electricity by shutting down industrial processes or adjusting tens of thousands of smart thermostats at once, effectively moving their electricity usage to a time when there is less demand. Voltus operates by offering incentives to companies to reduce their power consumption temporarily, and also offers inducements to electricity resellers that they can pass on to their customers.

items.title: Coforge Revenue Rises 54% as AI Engineering and Deal Bookings Gain Momentum
items.summary: Coforge reported a 53.6% year-on-year increase in consolidated revenue to ₹6,170.8 crore in Q2 FY27, supported by Encora's full-quarter contribution and the company’s continued focus on AI-led engineering . The IT services company also raised its FY27 EBIT margin guidance to 16%. Revenue increased 11.6% sequentially from ₹5,527.7 crore in Q1 FY27. Profit attributable to shareholders rose 13.4% quarter-on-quarter to ₹588.1 crore, compared with ₹518.6 crore in the previous quarter.

items.title: Siemens, Nvidia deploy industrial AI to reduce engineering effort
items.summary: The partners are using digital twins and AI agents as part of a roadmap to create world-first AI-powered manufacturing facilities.

items.title: OpenClaw creator spent $10 million on AI tokens last month
items.summary: OpenClaw, the AI digital assistant, is looking to establish itself as an essential tool for users — but if it is as profligate in its use of tokens as its creator, Pete Steinberger, then users could be in for some huge usage bills. Steinberger, now working for OpenAI , spent $10 million on AI tokens there last month, he told Cloudflare CEO Dane Knecht at the Cloudflare Connect 2026 Conference in San Francisco. ” Steinberger went on to question the adequacy of companies’ infrastructure, musing, “Why is this still using my computer? ” Adding cloud costs into the equation, as well as shoving privacy issues to one side would not reassure the audience.
